title: Customising the plot
text: Name property set heading. Without name, column name used:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Who took part" = "population", "design") )

title: Customising the plot
text: heatmap shows properties list, order list :
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Country" = "country", "Population" = "population") )

what: Order and names of the rows
title: Customising the plot
text: Rows follow order factor’s levels. Change order factor(..., levels = ...), rename levels labels = ...:
code: dat <- forestmap_example dat$population <- factor(   dat$population,   levels = c("Clinical", "Children", "Adults"),   labels = c("Clinical samples", "Children (< 18)", "Adults (18+)") )  plot_forestmap(   dat, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )

title: Customising the plot
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   y_label = "Hedges' g (95% CI)",   x_label = "Studies, sorted by effect size" )

title: Customising the plot
text: Colours depend whether confidence interval excludes value meaning “effect”. ’s 0 differences (log ratios) 1 ratios odds ratios. example effects converted odds ratios:  Ratios often easier read log scale: plot log() default null_value = 0.
code: odds <- forestmap_example odds$or <- exp(odds$smd * pi / sqrt(3)) odds$or_lower <- exp(odds$ci_lower * pi / sqrt(3)) odds$or_upper <- exp(odds$ci_upper * pi / sqrt(3))  plot_forestmap(   odds, "or", "or_lower", "or_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   null_value = 1,   y_label = "Odds ratio (95% CI)" )

what: Effects too small to matter: rope
title: Customising the plot
text: rope shades band effects consider small matter (“region practical equivalence”). Give two numbers, one number band symmetric around null_value:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   rope = c(-0.1, 0.1) )

title: Customising the plot
text: default y-axis symmetric around null_value wide enough show every confidence interval (ratios, starts 0). Set range y_limits; parts intervals outside cut :
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   y_limits = c(-1, 1.2) )

title: Customising the plot
text: Choose palette name. options "default" (shown examples ), "okabe_ito", "viridis" "greyscale". "okabe_ito" uses blue vermillion Okabe–Ito palette, designed stay distinguishable people common types colour blindness:  "viridis":  "greyscale", black--white printing:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   palette = "okabe_ito" ) plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   palette = "viridis" ) plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   palette = "greyscale" )

title: Customising the plot
text: Give three colours: positive effects, negative effects, effects whose interval includes null value. colour name hex code works:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   palette = c(positive = "#1b7837", negative = "#762a83", null = "grey75") )

title: Customising the plot
text: font takes name font installed computer. default "Arial Narrow" (plain sans-serif font isn’t installed). generic names "sans", "serif" "mono" work everywhere:  see fonts , run systemfonts::system_fonts()$family. can also use font file isn’t installed, giving path:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   font = "serif" ) plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   font = "fonts/MyFont-Regular.ttf" )

title: Customising the plot
text: text_size sets size text, points (default 9):
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   text_size = 12 )

title: Customising the plot
text: default, heatmap gets plot’s height rows . forest_height sets forest plot’s share height , 0 1. forest plot heatmap get half :
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design"),   forest_height = 0.5 )

title: Customising the plot
text: many properties levels heatmap gets tall. Two options help.

title: Customising the plot
text: layout = "compact" puts property’s name beside rows instead row :
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c(     "Population" = "population",     "Outcome measure" = "outcome",     "Study design" = "design",     "Country" = "country"   ),   layout = "compact" )

title: Customising the plot
text: max_levels sets rows property can . common levels kept, rest merged one “” row. max_levels = 3, five countries become USA, Australia :  several levels tie last place, kept get warning saying .
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c(     "Population" = "population",     "Outcome measure" = "outcome",     "Study design" = "design",     "Country" = "country"   ),   layout = "compact",   max_levels = 3 )

previous_headings: Going further with ggplot2 and patchwork
title: Customising the plot
text: Add line forest plot, example pooled effect meta-analysis. ’s simple inverse-variance (fixed-effect) average:  Text added annotate() doesn’t pick plot’s font automatically, set family font gave plot_forestmap().
code: se <- (forestmap_example$ci_upper - forestmap_example$ci_lower) / (2 * 1.96) pooled <- weighted.mean(forestmap_example$smd, w = 1 / se^2)  p <- plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )  p[[1]] <- p[[1]] +   ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = pooled, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +   ggplot2::annotate(     "text", x = 1, y = pooled, label = "Pooled effect",     hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6, size = 3, family = "sans"   ) p

previous_headings: Going further with ggplot2 and patchwork
title: Customising the plot
text: Change y-axis labels go scale_y_continuous(). Use round numbers; seq() can create tiny rounding errors show odd labels:
code: p <- plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )  p[[1]] <- p[[1]] + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1)) p

title: Customising the plot
text: plot_forestmap() doesn’t save anything; use ggplot2::ggsave() choose size . plot looks best around 7 × 5 inches four properties; add height add rows. PDFs, device = cairo_pdf makes sure fonts Arial Narrow work.
code: ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.png", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, dpi = 300) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.svg", p, width = 7, height = 5.25) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.pdf", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, device = cairo_pdf)

title: Getting started with forestmap
text: forest plot shows study meta-analysis effect size confidence interval. forestmap sorts studies smallest largest effect adds heatmap underneath showing study’s properties: population, design, country, anything else ’ve coded. Reading column tells one study; reading across row tells studies property fall among effects.

title: Getting started with forestmap
text: need data frame one row per study columns: package comes made-data 60 studies: order factor’s levels sets order rows heatmap, use factor(x, levels = ...) change . ’ve computed effect sizes metafor’s escalc(), gives study’s effect (yi) sampling variance (vi), add confidence interval like :
code: head(forestmap_example) #>         study   smd ci_lower ci_upper   n population     outcome #> 1   Wang 2005 0.470    0.223    0.716 253   Children        <NA> #> 2 Hughes 2013 0.261   -0.117    0.638 108   Children Behavioural #> 3  Rossi 2005 0.510    0.092    0.928  88     Adults Self-report #> 4  Baker 2006 0.410    0.170    0.649 268     Adults        <NA> #> 5 Hughes 2008 0.786    0.442    1.130 130   Children Self-report #> 6 Martin 2023 0.260   -0.234    0.754  63     Adults        <NA> #>               design   country #> 1                RCT       USA #> 2                RCT      <NA> #> 3 Quasi-experimental    Canada #> 4 Quasi-experimental Australia #> 5                RCT       USA #> 6                RCT       USA dat$ci_lower <- dat$yi - 1.96 * sqrt(dat$vi) dat$ci_upper <- dat$yi + 1.96 * sqrt(dat$vi)

title: Getting started with forestmap
text: Tell plot_forestmap() column . Naming study properties sets headings plot:
code: plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example,   es = "smd",   lb = "ci_lower",   ub = "ci_upper",   moderators = c(     "Population" = "population",     "Outcome measure" = "outcome",     "Study design" = "design",     "Country" = "country"   ) )

title: Getting started with forestmap
text: column one study. top panel shows effect 95% confidence interval; tiles show properties. Blue studies confidence interval entirely zero, red ones entirely , grey ones include zero. study’s tiles take colour. row tiles bunched one end means studies property tend find smaller (left) larger (right) effects. , every negative effect comes RCT, largest effects come mostly quasi-experimental studies using self-report measures.

title: Getting started with forestmap
text: plot_forestmap() returns plot; saving . Choose size save: many study properties, make plot taller (e.g. height = 10).
code: p <- plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example, "smd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",   moderators = c("Population" = "population", "Study design" = "design") )  ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.png", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, dpi = 300) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.svg", p, width = 7, height = 5.25) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.pdf", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, device = cairo_pdf)

title: Forest Plots with a Heatmap of Study Properties
text: need data frame one row per study: effect size, lower upper bounds 95% confidence interval, one factor column per study property. NA means study doesn’t report property. Tell plot_forestmap() columns . Name properties set headings shown plot.  Blue studies confidence interval entirely zero, red ones entirely , grey ones include zero. example, every study negative effect RCT, largest positive effects come mostly quasi-experimental studies using self-report measures. can change font, colours, text size, layout : see Customising plot. Saving , e.g.:
code: library(forestmap) head(forestmap_example) #>         study   smd ci_lower ci_upper   n population     outcome #> 1   Wang 2005 0.470    0.223    0.716 253   Children        <NA> #> 2 Hughes 2013 0.261   -0.117    0.638 108   Children Behavioural #> 3  Rossi 2005 0.510    0.092    0.928  88     Adults Self-report #> 4  Baker 2006 0.410    0.170    0.649 268     Adults        <NA> #> 5 Hughes 2008 0.786    0.442    1.130 130   Children Self-report #> 6 Martin 2023 0.260   -0.234    0.754  63     Adults        <NA> #>               design   country #> 1                RCT       USA #> 2                RCT      <NA> #> 3 Quasi-experimental    Canada #> 4 Quasi-experimental Australia #> 5                RCT       USA #> 6                RCT       USA plot_forestmap(   forestmap_example,   es = "smd",   lb = "ci_lower",   ub = "ci_upper",   moderators = c(     "Population" = "population",     "Outcome measure" = "outcome",     "Study design" = "design",     "Country" = "country"   ),   y_label = "SMD (95% CI)" ) p <- plot_forestmap(...) ggplot2::ggsave("forestmap.png", p, width = 7, height = 5.25, dpi = 300)

title: Forest plot of studies with a heatmap of study properties — plot_forestmap
code: plot_forestmap(   data,   es,   lb,   ub,   moderators,   font = "Arial Narrow",   palette = "default",   text_size = 9,   forest_height = "auto",   null_value = 0,   rope = NULL,   y_limits = NULL,   y_label = "Effect size",   x_label = "Effect",   max_levels = NULL,   layout = c("standard", "compact") )

title: Forest plot of studies with a heatmap of study properties — plot_forestmap
text: data data frame one row per study. es, lb, ub Names columns holding effect size lower upper bounds 95% confidence interval. moderators Names columns holding study properties (factors). Name vector set moderator's heading, e.g. c("Study design" = "design", "Population" = "population"); unnamed entries use column name. font font family installed computer (e.g. "Helvetica"), path .ttf/.otf font file. Defaults "Arial Narrow", falling back "sans" installed. palette palette name forestmap_palettes ("default", "okabe_ito", "viridis", "greyscale") three colours, e.g. c(positive = "darkgreen", negative = "purple", null = "grey"). text_size Base text size points. forest_height Share plot's height given forest plot (top panel), 0 1 (0.5 gives forest plot heatmap equal height). "auto" (default) gives heatmap room rows . null_value value meaning "effect": 0 differences log ratios, 1 raw ratios odds ratios. rope Optional region practical equivalence, drawn shaded band: two numbers c(-0.1, 0.1), one number band symmetric around null_value. y_limits Optional y-axis limits, e.g. c(-1, 1). default axis symmetric around null_value shows every confidence interval full; ratios (null_value 0 every value positive) starts 0. y_label, x_label Axis titles. max_levels Optional maximum number rows per moderator. max_levels = 3, 2 common levels shown rest merged one "" row. levels tie last place, kept (warning). NULL (default) shows every level. layout "standard" puts bold heading moderator's rows; "compact" puts moderator name left rows instead, makes heatmap shorter.

Options: standard compact layouts; built-("default", "okabe_ito", "viridis", "greyscale") custom palettes; custom fonts; automatic manual panel heights (forest_height); max_levels merge rare levels “”; rope, null_value y_limits.
